description: CERT.br, Brazil's national computer emergency response team for the internet, run by NIC.br, publishes statistics on the security incidents and threats it handles. The main series counts incident notifications voluntarily reported by security teams (CSIRTs), network administrators and users, updated monthly, with annual totals since 1999, notifications on devices taking part in denial-of-service attacks, a full table of monthly and annual totals, totals by category, the ports most often scanned or attacked, fraud attempt categories, and the top ten country codes and autonomous systems of attack sources. Further series cover phishing pages (time online and sectors affected), malicious DNS servers, misconfigured amplifiers abusable for DDoS, devices showing signs of compromise, vulnerable services exposed on the internet, the scans and attacks most often seen by CERT.br's honeypots, and spam complaints. Coverage: Brazil and networks notifying CERT.br. Format and access: web tables and charts on stats.cert.br, free under Creative Commons BY-NC-ND 4.0. Caveats: notifications are voluntary, so totals reflect reporting behaviour, not the full incidence of attacks; categories have changed over time. Simulation uses: frequency and type of cyber events against Brazilian networks, for scenario design and for exposure of internet services to DDoS and compromise. Related records: IX.br traffic statistics and the Anatel open data describe the networks themselves.
